mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.5% is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This is because low interest rates reduce the discount rate for equity valuations, increasing expected returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of instances where FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 9.5% signals a deteriorating labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This reflects investor concerns about economic recession and reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 9.5% (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 9.5% and industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90, it indicates a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where UNRATE > 9.5% and INDPRO < 90 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.5% within a 3-month window signals a monetary tightening cycle, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This reflects increased risk aversion and higher discount rates.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS has risen above 0.5% in the past 3 months (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) above 550 is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This reflects strong consumer demand and economic growth, boosting equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 550 (p-value < 0.05 for negative returns).

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 217.5 signals persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This reflects central bank tightening and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 217.5 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 90 and housing starts (HOUST) rises above 550, it indicates a supply-demand mismatch that leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO < 90 and HOUST > 550 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts (HOUST) below 500 and GDP (GDPC1) below 13190 signals a demand contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days. This reflects weak consumer and business spending, reducing equity growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where HOUST < 500 and GDPC1 < 13190 (p-value < 0.05 for positive returns).
